The rest of this page differentiates the soft 0-or-1 rule of the [machine learning review](ml-review.qmd#exr-log-loss-curve).
Among the images of 0s and 1s,
it gives each image the probability $\hprob = \sigmoidf{\predvar - \param}$ of being a 1,
where $\predvar$ is the image's center ink,
its average pixel over rows 2 to 5 and columns 3 and 4,
and $\param$ is the rule's cutoff.
Its mean [log loss](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/logistic-regression.html#def-log-loss) over those $\nobs$ images is

$$
\hR(\param) = -\frac{1}{\nobs} \sumin \sb{\outvar_i \log \hprob_i + (1 - \outvar_i) \log (1 - \hprob_i)},
$$

where $\outvar_i$ is 1 if image $i$ is a 1 and 0 if it is a 0.

```{python}
#| code-fold: show
center_ink = images[:, 2:6, 3:5].double().mean(dim=(1, 2))
is_01 = (labels == 0) | (labels == 1)
ink_01 = center_ink[is_01]
is_one = (labels[is_01] == 1).double()
n_01 = len(ink_01)
print(n_01)
print(ink_01[:5])
print(is_one[:5])
```

`.double()` stores the numbers as 64-bit floats,
so the comparisons below are not limited by 32-bit rounding.
